10. [Maximum mark: 30]
(i) In a $\triangle ABC$, D and E are points on the sides [BC] and [CA] such that DC = 2BD and EA = 2CE. If the lines (DE) and (AB) intersect at the point F, then prove that AB = 3BF. [4 marks]
(ii) (a) In a $\triangle ABC$, let D be the midpoint of the segment [BC] and [AD] be a median. Prove Apollonius' theorem, that $AB^2+AC^2=2(AD^2+BD^2)$. [5 marks]
(b) In a quadrilateral ABCD, X and Y are the midpoints of [AC] and [BD], respectively. Prove that $AB^2+BC^2+CD^2+DA^2=AC^2+BD^2+4XY^2$. [6 marks]
(iii) Let $F_1$ and $F_2$ be the foci of the ellipse whose equation is given by $\frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1,\ a>b$. Let P be the point on the ellipse with coordinates $(x_0, y_0)$ with $x_0, y_0>0$.
(a) Show that the equation of the tangent to the ellipse at the point P is given by $\frac{xx_0}{a^2}+\frac{yy_0}{b^2}=1$. [5 marks]
(b) The tangent at P meets the $x$-axis at the point M. Find the coordinates of point M. [2 marks]
(c) Find the lengths $PF_1, PF_2, MF_1, MF_2$. [4 marks]
(d) Use the converse of the angle bisector theorem to prove that [PM] is the external bisector of $F_2\hat{P}F_1$. [4 marks]
